To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NAFLD is a common metabolic disorder associated with T2DM, IR, and dyslipidemia.
NAFLD and T2DM are strongly associated with IR.
NAFLD is a hepatic manifestation of the metabolic syndrome and IR, and T2DM is a risk factor of NAFLD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of NAFLD and IR in T2DM and the role of antidiabetic drugs in the prevention and treatment of these metabolic diseases.
the complex and intricate interplay between IR, NAFLD, T2DM, and their clinical implications.
the intricate association between NAFLD, IR, and T2DM and the potential role of antidiabetic agents in the prevention of liver steatosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the association between NAFLD, IR, and T2DM is complex and multifactorial and that the current available antidiabetic drugs have limited efficacy in the treatment of NAFLD.
NAFLD is an early manifestation of IR and a risk factor for T2DM, and vice versa, and that IR is the common link between both diseases.
NAFLD is a common complication of T2DM and IR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NAFLD is the most prevalent liver disease, with a high prevalence in the T2DM patients.
the NAFLD and T2DM are strongly associated with each other and both conditions are mediated by IR.
IR is the main culprit for the development of both NAFLD and T2DM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NAFLD is a common complication of T2DM and vice versa, and the current antidiabetics have no beneficial effect on NAFLD, while new potential targets are being investigated.
IR and T2D are the common denominator in the development of NAFLD, which is also the main driver for the disease.
NAFLD should not be ignored in T2DM patients.
